Export of a file-owned suite writes `declaredId` as `suite.id`. Export of a
UI-owned suite derives a stable file
identity (`s_export_<sourceSuiteId>`),\nso importing the exported file creates a file-owned clone rather than\nre-claiming the ori

ginal UI suite.

When the run targets an **attached project environment** (`eval environments
set`), it executes against that e
nvironment's resolved host config, closed\nserver set, and pinned plugin versions instead of the suite's saved selection.\nEvery r
un records the environment and the exact revision it used, so `eval\nstatus` can answer \"which configuration did this run actuall

y execute against?"
long after the environment has been edited.

### `cloud eval server-facts`

Read the server a run was ta

ken against.

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--run <id>` | Yes | Eval run ID (from `eval run`) |
| `--pro
ject <id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID (defaults to the most recently updated project) |\n\nPer server: the tool count, the
catalog's measured size, annotation and\noutput-schema coverage, and the deterministic tool-metadata prechecks — plus\nwhat connec

t and discovery observed, and any conformance or readiness runs for
the same servers.

**None of it is a verdict.** A large too
l surface is not a defect and a slow\nconnect is not a failure; only a precheck with `class: \"spec_required\"` names a\nviolation

, and a row marked `protocolDependent` is a rule that may not apply to
this server's protocol version at all.

**Payload size i
s three different numbers** and this reports two of them, each\ncarrying its `payload.basis`: `aggregated_catalog_json` is the cat
alog as the\nclient assembled it (measured at capture), `normalized_snapshot` is what was\nretained after redaction — smaller, and
`payload.complete` says so. What the\nmodel actually saw is a host fact and is not here. Token figures are estimated\nas `json_ch

ars_div_4` against a **reference** window, not measured against any
model's real context.

Server facts are computed on read, s
o there is no backfill window: a run that\nfinished long ago still answers. A run with nothing to describe answers inside\nthe doc
ument with `state: \"unavailable\"` and a reason — `snapshotMissing`,\n`snapshotPartial` (the servers that answered are still list

ed, and their numbers
are real), or `setupNotObserved` (unmeasured, **not** failed).

Related conformance and readiness runs ar
e joined by **server id alone**, so a\ndifferent server version, environment or auth context is not excluded by the\nmatch. Each c

arries its own timestamp, and none of them is this run's verdict.

### `cloud eval status`

Get the status and summary of an e

val run.

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--run <id>` | Yes | Eval run ID (from `eval run`) |
| `--project
<id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID (defaults to the most recently updated project) |\n| `--diagnostics-limit <n>` | No | Fai
lure diagnostics per page (1–200; default 20) |\n| `--diagnostics-cursor <cursor>` | No | Cursor from a previous response's `decis
ionSummary.diagnostics.nextCursor` |\n| `--stages` | No | Print all six user-value chain rows for each failing trial (`--format hu

man`) |

The response carries a `judges` block with each advisory grader's state and
per-case grades. `status: null` means that
judge was never requested for the\nrun — different from a judge that ran and graded nothing. In `--format human`,\neach judge tha

t actually graded gets a one-line summary.

Goal completion reports per-iteration `status`: `scored`, `error`, or `skipped`.
Le
gacy scored rows are returned as `scored`. A failed job retains completed\nmeasurements alongside any unscored error or skipped ro
ws; job failure does not\nmean every trial failed its goal. Use each row's `status` before interpreting\n`score` and `passed`, and
join rows to trials using `iterationId`.\nPending jobs return an empty `cases` array and may expose `progress`\n(`total`, `comple
ted`, `errors`, `skipped`). Terminal jobs may include template\nversion/hash; case rows may also include `gradingKey`, `errorCode`
,\n`evidenceHash`, and `evidenceManifest` for provenance. Older results can omit\nthese fields. Groundedness retains its existing

per-case grade shape.

The failure diagnostics inside `decisionSummary` are **paginated**, and a page
that is not the whole set
says so: `diagnostics.complete` is `false` and\n`diagnostics.nextCursor` carries the next page. Without `--diagnostics-cursor`\na
run with more failures than the page size reports only its first 20, so a\nscript that concludes \"only these failed\" from one p

age is reading a sample.
Walk the pages:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam cloud eval status --run "$RUN_ID
\" --diagnostics-limit 200 --format json\n# then, while .decisionSummary.diagnostics.complete is false:\nmcpjam cloud eval status
--run \"$RUN_ID\" --diagnostics-limit 200 \\\n --diagnostics-cursor \"$NEXT_CURSOR\" --format json\n", "exit_code": 0, "status":
"completed"}}
